understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete KA59 by solving each level within its step budget, where a level is won only when every goal tile marked '+' is simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece (one selectable per goal), and progressing through all levels until the final WIN ends the run.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN to shift the currently selected piece by one grid cell (3 pixels) per action in that direction, unless blocked by walls/boundaries or interactions. Some adjacent objects could be pushable blocks that move along if pushed, while walls ('#') generally prevent movement though some boundary/wall behaviors could be non-uniform and needed experimentation. Levels could contain multiple selectable pieces; CLICK with an exact [x, y] pixel-coordinate matching a selectable's position switched which piece was controlled. The movement.*_blocked flags were only hints about adjacent objects and did not guarantee failure or success; actual outcomes had to be tested with actions.

understanding.goal_understanding: The goal was to complete KA59 by solving each level within its step budget, where a level is won only when every goal tile marked '+' is simultaneously occupied by a selectable piece (one selectable per goal), and progressing through all levels until the final WIN ends the run.
understanding.mechanics_understanding: Movement used MOVE_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN to shift the currently selected piece by one grid cell (3 pixels) per action in that direction, unless blocked by walls/boundaries or interactions. Some adjacent objects could be pushable blocks that move along if pushed, while walls ('#') generally prevent movement though some boundary/wall behaviors could be non-uniform and needed experimentation. Levels could contain multiple selectable pieces; CLICK with an exact [x, y] pixel-coordinate matching a selectable's position switched which piece was controlled. The movement.*_blocked flags were only hints about adjacent objects and did not guarantee failure or success; actual outcomes had to be tested with actions.
